topic.title: Adaptive Reasoning Computation and Inference Control
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Reasoning models can spend substantial computation on long intermediate sequences. This topic studies when to continue reasoning, how to organize independent subproblems, and which internal state must be retained. A representative framework trains models to interleave planning with parallel execution, reducing sequential work while preserving task performance in its evaluations.
topic.whyItMatters: Longer reasoning is not always more useful, and unnecessary steps increase latency and memory use. Effective control must estimate whether extra computation is likely to improve the answer without prematurely stopping difficult problems or disrupting essential dependencies.
topic.evolution: The representatives include earlier memory-based and abstract reasoning alongside recent language-model methods. Newer papers focus on adaptive stopping, difficulty estimation, parallel reasoning, instruction-following failures, and attention-head-aware cache compression. Together they investigate where computation contributes to reasoning quality.
openQuestions: How can a model predict the marginal value of further reasoning?
Which reasoning dependencies can be parallelized or compressed without introducing difficult-to-detect errors?

papers.title: Statistical Early Stopping for Reasoning Models
papers.tldr: Statistical stopping rules use uncertainty during generation to reduce excessive reasoning, with especially strong reported gains in mathematics.

papers.title: Step-Level Sparse Autoencoder for Reasoning Process Interpretation
papers.tldr: SSAE extracts sparse reasoning-step features that predict properties including correctness and logicality, suggesting partial internal information relevant to self-verification.

papers.title: Stop When Further Reasoning Won’t Help: Attention-State Adaptive Generation in Reasoning Models
papers.tldr: ASAG uses attention distributions to adaptively stop reasoning, improving reported accuracy while substantially reducing generated tokens without additional training.

papers.title: Strategy-Aware Optimization Modeling with Reasoning LLMs
papers.tldr: SAGE explicitly trains optimization-modeling strategies, improving first-attempt success, formulation diversity, and constraint compactness.

papers.title: Strategy Executability in Mathematical Reasoning: Leveraging Human–Model Differences for Effective Guidance
papers.tldr: Selective Strategy Retrieval improves mathematical guidance by choosing strategies a target model can effectively execute.

papers.title: Structure Enables Effective Self-Localization of Errors in LLMs
papers.tldr: Structuring reasoning into complete thoughts improves error localization and supports correction by backtracking to the last correct step.

papers.title: SubspacePath Pruner: Inference-time Pruning via Probe-based Representation–Parameter Coupling
papers.tldr: SubspacePath Pruner builds scenario-specific subnetworks with a reported 1.27-fold speedup, improving cross-domain Recall but reducing cross-dataset Recall.

papers.title: SuCo: Sufficiency-guided Continuous Adaptive Reasoning
papers.tldr: SuCo trains reasoning models to adapt their effort around sufficient reasoning, improving both accuracy and token efficiency in the evaluated tasks.

papers.title: TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems
papers.tldr: TFRBench tests forecasting reasoning and shows that verified, numerically grounded reasoning traces can improve LLM forecasting accuracy.

papers.title: TG-RAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Reasoning Guidance in Specialized Domains
papers.tldr: TG-RAG uses a procedure graph and an Interrupt-Retrieve-Generate cycle to guide reasoning models through specialized workflows.

papers.title: The Deterministic Horizon: When Extended Reasoning Fails and Tool Delegation Becomes Necessary
papers.tldr: The paper finds depth-dependent failures in deterministic state tracking and evidence that tool delegation can outperform extended unaided reasoning.

papers.title: The Flexibility Trap: Rethinking the Value of Arbitrary Order in Diffusion Language Models
papers.tldr: JustGRPO improves diffusion-model reasoning by dropping arbitrary generation order while retaining parallel decoding.

papers.title: The Geometric Reasoner: Manifold-Informed Latent Foresight Search for Long-Context Reasoning
papers.tldr: TGR guides training-free reasoning search with latent foresight and geometric regularization, improving trajectory coverage under chunk-based memory bounds.

papers.title: The Geometry of Reasoning: Self-Evaluation via Layerwise Trajectory Evolution
papers.tldr: GeoR evaluates reasoning correctness through layerwise hidden-state geometry calibrated for query uncertainty.

papers.title: The Quality-Utility Paradox: Why High-Reward Data Impairs Small Model Mathematical Reasoning
papers.tldr: Higher-scoring mathematical traces can teach small models less effectively when their style drifts from the learner’s native reasoning distribution.

papers.title: The Shadow Price of Reasoning: Economic Perspective on Optimal Budget Allocation for LLMs
papers.tldr: CLEAR allocates reasoning tokens using a global shadow price, improving workload-level accuracy under constrained computation budgets.

papers.title: The Signal is in the Steps: Local Scoring for Reasoning Data Selection
papers.tldr: LALP selects reasoning data by scoring local step transitions, improving student accuracy when learning from diverse teachers.

papers.title: The Tell-Tale Norm: $\ell_2$ Magnitude as a Signal for Reasoning Dynamics in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Hidden-state L2 norms indicate reasoning intensity and guide inference-time techniques that improve reasoning without additional training or data.

papers.title: Think-at-Hard: Dynamic Looped Transformers for Improved Reasoning
papers.tldr: Think-at-Hard improves reasoning by selectively refining difficult tokens, avoiding extra iterations that can overturn correct predictions.

papers.title: Think Deep, Not Just Long: Measuring LLM Reasoning Effort via Deep-Thinking Tokens
papers.tldr: Deep-layer prediction revisions provide a stronger reported accuracy signal than response length and enable cheaper reasoning-sample selection.

papers.title: Think in Latent, Explain in Language: Self-Explainable Latent Reasoning
papers.tldr: SELR jointly trains a model to reason through compact embeddings and decode them into explanations, improving reported accuracy and token efficiency.

papers.title: Thinking in Flow: A Dissipative Stabilization Operator for Robust Autoregressive Reasoning
papers.tldr: Thinking in Flow uses a gated Neural ODE controller to stabilize reasoning trajectories and improve measured robustness to distracting or perturbed context.

papers.title: ThoughtFold: Folding Reasoning Chains via Introspective Preference Learning
papers.tldr: ThoughtFold trains models to remove redundant reasoning segments, cutting one model’s token use by about 56% while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy.

papers.title: ThreadWeaver: Adaptive Threading for Efficient Parallel Reasoning in Language Models
papers.tldr: ThreadWeaver trains adaptive parallel reasoning that matches comparable sequential models' math accuracy with up to 1.53 times faster token latency.

papers.title: Time Series Reasoning via Process-Verifiable Thinking Data Synthesis and Scheduling for Tailored LLM Reasoning
papers.tldr: VeriTime combines verifiable time-series reasoning data, structured scheduling, and tailored reinforcement learning to strengthen compact language models.

papers.title: ToMAP: Training Opponent-Aware LLM Persuaders with Theory of Mind
papers.tldr: ToMAP improves model-based persuasion by anticipating objections and predicting how strongly the other participant agrees with them.

papers.title: Towards Efficient Large Language Reasoning Models via Extreme-Ratio Chain-of-Thought Compression
papers.tldr: Extra-CoT combines semantically preserved compression, mixed-budget fine-tuning, and hierarchical reinforcement learning to shorten mathematical reasoning while maintaining answer quality.

papers.title: Towards Long-Horizon Interpretability: Efficient and Faithful Multi-Token Attribution for Reasoning LLMs
papers.tldr: FlashTrace accelerates multi-token attribution and improves faithfulness by recursively tracing importance through reasoning back to source inputs.

papers.title: TRACE: Toulmin-based Reasoning Assessment through Constructive Elements for LLM CoT Evaluation
papers.tldr: TRACE evaluates the structure of LLM reasoning, correlates with answer accuracy, and improves training results when used as a reinforcement-learning reward.

papers.title: TSRBench: A Comprehensive Multi-task Multi-modal Time Series Reasoning Benchmark for Generalist Models
papers.tldr: TSRBench reveals gaps between time-series reasoning and forecasting, alongside ineffective fusion of textual and visual inputs in current generalist models.

papers.title: Turning Drift into Constraint: Robust Reasoning Alignment in Non-Stationary Multi-Stream Environments
papers.tldr: APO uses changing disagreements among source models as negative constraints to improve reasoning alignment under drift.

papers.title: Uncovering the Gradient Geometry of Long CoT: A Spectral-guided Approach to Reasoning Distillation
papers.tldr: Spectral-guided Learning prioritizes reasoning steps whose gradients align with shared low-rank directions, improving student-model robustness and generalization.

papers.title: Universal Reasoner: A Single, Composable Plug-and-Play Reasoner for Frozen LLMs
papers.tldr: UniR trains composable reasoning modules whose logits guide frozen language models, including larger models within the same family.

papers.title: V1: Unifying Generation and Self-Verification for Parallel Reasoners
papers.tldr: V1 improves parallel reasoning through uncertainty-guided pairwise comparisons and joint training of generation and self-verification.

papers.title: Verifying Meta-Awareness via Predictive Rewards in Reasoning Models
papers.tldr: MAPR trains models to predict and verify their own reasoning statistics, improving reported mathematical accuracy and training efficiency.

papers.title: Wait, Wait, Wait... Why Do Reasoning Models Loop?
papers.tldr: Learning errors and temporally correlated mistakes help explain reasoning-model loops, while higher temperature provides only partial relief.

papers.title: What Characterizes Effective Reasoning? Revisiting Length, Review, and Structure of CoT
papers.tldr: The fraction of reasoning spent on abandoned branches predicts correctness better than length or review frequency and guides interventions that improve accuracy.

papers.title: What Makes Effective Supervision in Latent Chain-of-Thought: An Information-Theoretic Analysis
papers.tldr: An information-theoretic analysis links latent reasoning accuracy to preserved reasoning information and motivates complementary trajectory and semantic supervision.

papers.title: What Really Improves Mathematical Reasoning: Structured Reasoning Signals Beyond Pure Code
papers.tldr: Controlled experiments find limited broad reasoning transfer from code and stronger, difficulty-dependent benefits from specific structured reasoning signals.

papers.title: When LLMs Develop Languages: Symbolic Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.tldr: CLSR evolves and routes compact symbolic communication protocols, reducing reported reasoning-token use three- to sixfold while maintaining accuracy.

papers.title: When Simple Problems Wear Complex Costumes: Improving Efficiency in LRM’s Adaptive Reasoning
papers.tldr: Two-stage training helps adaptive reasoning models avoid unnecessary reasoning when simple problems are phrased verbosely.

papers.title: When to Think, When to Speak: Learning Disclosure Policies for LLM Reasoning
papers.tldr: Side-by-Side trains models to disclose supported answer portions during continued reasoning, improving measured accuracy–content-latency tradeoffs.

papers.title: Which Heads Matter for Reasoning? RL-Guided KV Cache Compression
papers.tldr: RLKV learns which attention heads need full memory, enabling 20–60% cache reduction with near-lossless reasoning performance.
